A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DyGPrompt. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and matchable despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification and link-prediction experiments, component ablations, embedding visualizations, and label-abundant results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons and supplementary experiments in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.5 retain the same pre-training objective, feature and time prompts, dual condition-nets, and prompt tuning with frozen DGNN weights.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Wikipedia, Reddit, and MOOC on temporal node classification and transductive and inductive link prediction. Label-scarce and label-abundant coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Tables 1 and 5, including ROLAND variants, dynamic GNNs, DDGCL, CPDG, GraphPrompt, and TIGPrompt variants.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the chronological 80% pre-training allocation, 1%/1%/18% downstream split, 30-event training sample, negative sampling, and evaluation metrics. Appendix E's label-abundant protocol also matches.

E4.justification: Figure 3 revises the qualitative evidence in the embedding case study by exchanging the Reddit/DyGPrompt and MOOC/without-prompts plots. The analysis question and sampling description remain unchanged, as do the component ablations, backbone comparisons, and sensitivity study.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 sampled tasks with five random seeds each and averages and standard deviations over 500 results. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 3 moves the more separated plot from MOOC/without prompts to Reddit/DyGPrompt and moves the mixed plot in the opposite direction, changing the qualitative findings attributed to those conditions. Numerical results in Tables 1–3 and 5 and Figure 4 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The dynamic-graph definitions and mathematical formulations in Equations 1–12 are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical results or proofs in its appendices.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about bridging task and temporal gaps, modeling mutual node-time dependencies, and outperforming baselines on three datasets.

C2.justification: The result interpretations, including Section 5.3's claim of improved embedding separation, are unchanged. Appendix A retains the limitation that pre-training uses only dynamic graphs and proposes incorporating static graphs.

D1.justification: Appendices B and D retain the same dataset links, baseline implementation information, optimizer, hardware, dimensions, and neighbor-sampling details. Dataset-link footnotes are only renumbered.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 46 references are unchanged, including the positioning against static graph prompting and TIGPrompt.

P1.justification: v4 adds first-page footnotes explaining equal contribution, work performed at Singapore Management University, and corresponding authorship. Scientific prose, terminology, and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 exchanges two existing panels while retaining its labels and caption. Author footnotes and subsequent text reflow alter spacing and page breaks, leaving the conclusion's final lines on a largely empty page 10.

improvement.justification: v4 clarifies author roles and makes Figure 3 more consistent with the unchanged discussion. However, neither PDF explains the exchange between Reddit/DyGPrompt and MOOC/without prompts, so whether it corrects or introduces misattribution cannot be established. With methods, numerical results, and appendices otherwise unchanged, a reliable overall quality improvement is uncertain.
